title: The conformal dimension of the Brownian sphere is two
summary: The conformal dimension of a metric space $(X, d)$ is equal to the infimum of the Hausdorff dimensions among all metric spaces quasisymmetric to $(X, d)$. It is an important quasisymmetric invariant which lies non-strictly between the topological and Hausdorff dimensions of $(X, d)$. We consider the conformal dimension of the Brownian sphere (a.k.a. the Brownian map), whose law can be thought of as the uniform measure on metric measure spaces homeomorphic to the standard sphere $\mathbf S^2$ with unit area.
